item.research_question: How can a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film with superior mechanical and tribological properties be synthesized using a cost-effective single target, and what are the effects of annealing on its adhesion and wear performance?
item.material_system: Equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates
item.processing_route: DC-magnetron sputtering using a single target prepared by partial spark plasma sintering (SPS) of equimolar elemental powders (Cu, Mo, Ta, W, V) at 1000 °C under 40 MPa pressure; film deposition at 500 °C substrate temperature for 120 min in Ar atmosphere (1.16 × 10⁻³ mPa, 150 W power); post-deposition annealing at 300 °C for adhesion improvement
item.test_conditions: Nanoindentation at 3 mN load; nanopillar compression (440 nm diameter, 3 mN max force); tribological wear tests at room temperature (RT) and 300 °C with 1 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed against E52100 alloy steel counterballs
key_findings: The as-deposited film exhibited a nanocrystalline body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution with an average grain size of 18 nm and a thickness of ~900 nm.
Nanoindentation measurements yielded an average hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.
Nanopillar compression tests on 440-nm pillars revealed a high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa.
Annealing at 300 °C reduced surface roughness to 2 nm (Sa) and significantly improved film adhesion compared to the as-deposited state.
The annealed film showed an average coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.25 at RT and 1.5 at 300 °C.
Wear rates for the annealed film were 6.4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N m at RT and 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N m at 300 °C.
The COF of the RHEA film was 2 times lower at RT and the wear rate was 10² times lower at both RT and 300 °C compared to 304 stainless steel.
The film showed intergranular fracture behavior during compression, attributed to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation.
item.mechanism: The high hardness and strength are attributed to the combined effects of solid solution hardening, grain boundary strengthening due to nanocrystallinity (18 nm), and lattice distortion. The shift from dislocation-controlled to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation in the nanopillars leads to intergranular fracture. Annealing improves adhesion by refining grains and reducing surface roughness, while the formation of CuO at 300 °C contributes to the tribological behavior.
item.limitations: The study notes that the as-deposited film suffered from low adhesion, leading to excessive plastic deformation, smearing, and film removal during wear tests at room temperature. Additionally, the coefficient of friction increased significantly at 300 °C due to tribochemical reactions and oxide formation on the counterball.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the study may lead to the processing of high-entropy alloy films for large-scale industrial applications, particularly in wear-resistant applications such as aerospace, milling inserts, and cutting tools.
quotes: A high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa was obtained in nanopillar compression due to solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.
The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.
The COF was found to be 2 times lower at RT and wear rate 10 2 times lower at RT and 300 °C than those of 304 stainless steel.
